438	**technique.** Session-level stopping rule as a finite-horizon MDP with exact replay: stop trading for the day after k stop-outs or a loss L, tested against the null that the session ledger so far carries no information about the next SETUP
439	
440	**what_it_answers.** Whether the causal session ledger (today_net_asof, today_n_stops_asof, today_n_setups_before; 1m median 8 SETUPs per active session, max 20) predicts the next SETUP's net at all, and whether a daily stop rule adds expectancy beyond the cost it saves by trading less (the pure cost-avoidance trap in its simplest form).

442	**method.** State at each SETUP: (today_n_stops_asof, today_net_asof bucket, today_n_setups_before, hour_bin) plus the study-1 score. Null test first: permutation of SETUP order within each session (2,000 draws) for the correlation between today_net_asof and the next fnd_net and for the difference in mean net after >= k stops vs fewer; if the null is not rejected on IS the study ends with "no session memory" and no key. If rejected: finite-horizon DP by exact replay over the small grid k in {1,2,3,4}, L in {-2,000, -4,000, -6,000, none} INR, optional re-arm after a winner; value = kept-minus-skipped expectancy (never net), session-matched random control at the same per-session k (this rule is a within-session gate, so the standard control applies directly), permutation p. Keep seven, merged into five lines of work, about 1-1.5 CPU-hours per timeframe in total: (1) one validation harness = quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's SPA, adversarial drift and 5m null tapes folded in (one ledger, one bootstrap, one PBO, active sessions only, every comparator re-priced on the L1 15:25 label); (2) one feature-vocabulary pass = quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, its 8-cluster shortlist frozen in the ledger before any gate search, with BOCPD, FFD and the novelty scalars entering there and nowhere else; (3) one learned-gate family = quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate and decision-making-1 merged (L1 label, capped |net| weights, top-1%-winners-removed as a hard pass, block-wise sign test, one distilled rule list or scorecard as the single OOS candidate from the family); (4) the interpretable candidate = deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses with a blind round 0 from the user's words alone, hashed before any table is shown, and cross-fitted round-1 tables; (5) the cheap desk rule = decision-making-6 session stop with an hour-conditioned null. That yields at most three OOS looks: the rule list from (3), the round-0 list from (4), and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator, with (5) as a multiplication if its null is rejected.
- Why this lens splits the problem the way it does. (1) The take/skip choice at a Foundation SETUP is a contextual bandit with FULL information: Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of "take" (fnd_net, 1m: 5,326 rows, 5m: 1,012 rows) is logged for every context, and the reward of "skip" is exactly 0 by definition. There is no unobserved arm, hence no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction: the off-policy value of ANY gate pi is computed exactly as sum over SETUPs of pi(x)*net(x). The only statistical problem is generalisation from a few thousand contexts, so the right tools are cost-sensitive policy learning (value-maximising policy trees, cost-proportionate weighting) and honest selection, not bandit exploration. (2) Sequential RL is genuinely justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable: the in-trade exit (hold/exit/partial each bar; 1m IS has ~186k intraday bar-steps inside positions, ~800k once trajectories are extended to the 15:25 square-off) and, at session level, whether to keep trading today. On a price-taker's tape the dynamics are exogenous (an Exo-MDP): any exit policy can be replayed exactly and the hindsight-optimal exit is computable per trade, so OPE (DR/MAGIC) is not the bottleneck; generalisation and multiplicity are. Deep offline RL (CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer) and neural generators (TimeGAN, diffusion) are not runnable here (no torch) and would be badly over-parameterised for 4.5k trajectories anyway; the studies say so and use the closest feasible analogues (pessimistic tree-ensemble FQI, hindsight-imitation, GMM-Markov and session-bootstrap tapes). (3) Sizing is a downstream Kelly problem that only exists once a positive-conditional-edge region is found; the raw book (win rate 15%, mean -922 INR) has negative Kelly, and the study is written to return "0 lots" honestly. (4) Costs are 1,050-1,120 INR per trade and the median 1m trade moves 9 pts, so a gate that trades less always raises net by the saved costs: every study judges on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, the session-matched random control at the same per-session position count (fz_report.random_control), the permutation p, and (new here) the multiplicity-adjusted SPA/PBO from session-block resampling. (5) Leakage discipline is shared: features from the as-of columns only (prefixes fnd_, fwd_, fzpos_, st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones/visits final-state fields are excluded), contiguous session-block CV with purge (drop training trades whose exit falls in the test block) and a 2-session embargo, OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) touched once per study at the end; the 5-minute engine trades are re-cut at 15:25 from bars because the build carries no square-off (358 of 1,012 held overnight). Priority order: the gate (1), the exit policy (2), then the robustness/multiplicity certificate that must pass before any key ships (3), the certified operating point (4), sizing (5), the session-stop rule (6). Compute: every study fits in one process under 1 GB; the two heavy jobs (1m FQI ensemble, 1m synthetic tapes) must not run concurrently with each other because each peaks near 900 MB.

BOS, prot, swings), Foundation trades with pts/net/exit (net = pts x 65 minus 1,114 INR costs for 1m, minus 5-minute-appropriate costs: use lab.trade_charges with ZERODHA_NFO_FUT and slippage 5 pts per side), fz.run card + ledger with the ST7 (1m) / ST8 (5m) fz block (thresholds from strategies/strategy_7.json / strategy_8.json), and the feature table per SETUP (columns documented in a README.md next to the files). 29	1. **"Ensure to use latest AI and machine-learning techniques to understand the patterns and come up with how to trade in this."** The classical H1-H5 program above is the floor, not the ceiling. ST5-ST8 stay frozen; nothing in `engine.py` changes; no trading number in code (every threshold, weight file path and learner hyper-parameter is a strategy-file key with a `source`).
31	3. **"Ensure not to take shortcuts or skip best analysis or modelling or training due to hardware constraint; if that's the call then move to Claude cloud by committing required files."** The four input files are committed under `fz_v3/data/` for that reason. 32	4. **"Even incorporate journal every trade and induce reinforcement learning after each trade to optimize strategy, money management and profit factor."** Two requirements:
33	   - **Trade journal.** One row per Foundation SETUP (taken or skipped) and per closed trade: timestamp, direction, the full feature vector at the decision bar (card fields, regime, volume, level context, time), the policy's decision and its stated reason, the policy's state id (which model / which update it was made with), fill, exit reason, MFE / MAE, pts, gross, costs, net, R-multiple, and the running book (equity, drawdown, rolling profit factor). This journal is the training set of the online learner and the audit trail of every decision. In the lab build it is a table the strategy writes (`fz_journal.csv` or a `journal` block in the results), never a side effect hidden in code.
34	   - **Learning after each trade (online / walk-forward).** The policy used at trade t is fitted only on journal rows of trades closed before t (strictly causal; anchored or rolling window as a config key), and is refitted after every closed trade (or every k trades, k a key). 100	def recompute_ledger(net, stop, sess_first, sess_run):
101	    """The ledger before each position from a (possibly permuted) outcome sequence: cumulative sum / count within the session."""
102	    prior_net = np.cumsum(net) - net; prior_stop = np.cumsum(stop.astype(int)) - stop.astype(int)
103	    return prior_net - prior_net[sess_first][sess_run], prior_stop - prior_stop[sess_first][sess_run]

106	def stats7(today_net, today_stops, net):
107	    """The seven pre-registered statistics (nan when a side is empty)."""
108	    out = np.full(7, np.nan)
109	    rx, ry = sst.rankdata(today_net), sst.rankdata(net)
110	    if rx.std() > 0 and ry.std() > 0: out[0] = np.corrcoef(rx, ry)[0, 1]
111	    for j, k in enumerate(K_TESTS):
112	        m = today_stops >= k
113	        if m.any() and (~m).any(): out[1 + j] = net[m].mean() - net[~m].mean()
114	    for j, L in enumerate(L_TESTS):
115	        m = today_net <= L
116	        if m.any() and (~m).any(): out[4 + j] = net[m].mean() - net[~m].mean()
117	    return out

120	def holm(p):
121	    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float); m = len(p); order = np.argsort(p); adj = np.empty(m); run = 0.0
122	    for rank, i in enumerate(order):
123	        run = max(run, min(1.0, (m - rank) * p[i])); adj[i] = run
124	    return adj

127	def null_test(S, tf, label, null, draws=NULL_DRAWS):
128	    """Permute outcomes within cells (N1: session x hour_bin; N2: session), recompute the ledger, redo the 7 statistics."""
129	    cell = S["cell_run"] if null == "session_x_hour" else S["sess_run"]
130	    obs = stats7(S["today_net"], S["today_stops"], S["net"])
131	    rng = rng_for(tf, label, null)
132	    perm_stats = np.empty((draws, 7))
133	    for d in range(draws):
134	        perm = np.lexsort((rng.random(len(cell)), cell))                 # within each contiguous cell, a random order
135	        pn, ps = S["net"][perm], S["stop"][perm]
136	        tn, ts = recompute_ledger(pn, ps, S["sess_first"], S["sess_run"])
137	        perm_stats[d] = stats7(tn, ts, pn)
138	    valid = np.isfinite(perm_stats); n_valid = valid.sum(axis=0)
139	    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
140	        lo = (1 + ((perm_stats <= obs[None, :] + 1e-12) & valid).sum(axis=0)) / (1 + n_valid)
141	        hi = (1 + ((perm_stats >= obs[None, :] - 1e-12) & valid).sum(axis=0)) / (1 + n_valid)
142	        p_abs = (1 + ((np.abs(perm_stats) >= np.abs(obs)[None, :] - 1e-12) & valid).sum(axis=0)) / (1 + n_valid)
143	    p = np.minimum(1.0, 2 * np.minimum(lo, hi))
144	    cells = np.bincount(cell)
145	    return dict(null=null, draws=draws, observed=obs, p=p, p_holm=holm(p), p_lo=lo, p_hi=hi, p_abs=p_abs, perm_mean=np.nanmean(perm_stats, axis=0),
146	                perm_sd=np.nanstd(perm_stats, axis=0), perm_valid=n_valid, excess=obs - np.nanmean(perm_stats, axis=0),
147	                n_cells=int(len(cells)), cells_size1=int((cells == 1).sum()), rows_movable=int(cells[cells > 1].sum()))

206	def running_min_by_session(x, sess_first, sess_run):
207	    out = np.empty_like(x)
208	    for s in range(len(sess_first)):
209	        a = sess_first[s]; b = sess_first[s + 1] if s + 1 < len(sess_first) else len(x)
210	        out[a:b] = np.minimum.accumulate(x[a:b])

214	def grid_keep(today_stops, today_net_runmin, k, L):
215	    """Absorbing rule: skip once the session's ledger at the bar has >= k stops or its running minimum net <= L."""
216	    stopped = today_stops >= k
217	    if L is not None: stopped = stopped | (today_net_runmin <= L)
218	    return ~stopped

221	def rearm_keep(net, stop, sess_first, sess_run, k, L):
222	    """Re-arm after a winner: while armed, take and count (stops, net since the last arm); stop when the count reaches >= k stops
223	    or <= L; while stopped, skip, and re-arm at the next SETUP (counters reset) when the skipped SETUP's paper trade wins."""
224	    n = len(net); keep = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
225	    for s in range(len(sess_first)):
226	        a = sess_first[s]; b = sess_first[s + 1] if s + 1 < len(sess_first) else n
227	        armed, ns, nn = True, 0, 0.0
228	        for j in range(a, b):
229	            if armed:
230	                keep[j] = True; ns += int(stop[j]); nn += net[j]
231	                if ns >= k or (L is not None and nn <= L): armed = False
232	            else:
233	                keep[j] = False
234	                if net[j] > 0: armed, ns, nn = True, 0, 0.0
235	    return keep

243	    """Keep masks over T's rows for every grid cell, built from the IS rows only (the rule reads the built as-of ledger; the rearm

256	def choose_cell(T, masks, tr):
257	    """Training-fold choice: the cell with the largest kept-vs-skipped diff among cells with kept_share >= 0.20; tie -> larger kept share."""
258	    best = None
259	    for key, m in masks.items():
260	        r = H.metrics(T, m, tr, tag="train", controls=False)
261	        if r["kept_share"] is None or r["kept_share"] < KEPT_SHARE_FLOOR or r["diff"] is None: continue
262	        cand = (r["diff"], r["kept_share"], key)
263	        if best is None or cand > best: best = cand
264	    return best

267	def branch_b(T, tf, out):
268	    log(f"[{tf}] branch B: the {len(all_cells())}-cell grid, nested choice, CPCV, go/no-go")
269	    masks = cell_masks(T); is_rows = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
270	    grid_rows, vecs, keys = [], [], []
271	    for key, m in masks.items():
272	        cfg = json.loads(key)
273	        r = H.score(T, m, f"{STUDY}/grid", cfg, script=__file__)
274	        grid_rows.append(r); vecs.append(H.session_vectors(T, m, is_rows)); keys.append(key)
275	        log(f"  grid {cfg}: id {r['id']} kept {r['kept_n']} share {r['kept_share']} diff {r['diff']} ctrl {r['control_pct']} perm_p {r['perm_p']}")
276	    pd.DataFrame(grid_rows).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, f"grid_{tf}.csv"), index=False)
277	    # nested choice inside the 12 purged training folds -> one OOF mask
278	    oof = np.zeros(T.n, dtype=bool); chosen_folds = []
279	    for b, (tr, te) in enumerate(H.purged_splits(T)):
280	        best = choose_cell(T, masks, tr)
281	        if best is None: chosen_folds.append(None); oof[te] = True; continue
282	        oof[te] = masks[best[2]][te]; chosen_folds.append(json.loads(best[2]))
283	    nested = H.score(T, oof, f"{STUDY}/nested", dict(selection="max diff | kept_share>=0.20 in training fold", folds=12), script=__file__)
284	    log(f"  nested OOF: id {nested['id']} kept {nested['kept_n']} diff {nested['diff']} ctrl {nested['control_pct']} perm_p {nested['perm_p']} sign_blocks {nested['sign_blocks']}")
285	    # CPCV: 66 splits -> 11 paths
286	    oof_split = {}
287	    for tr, te, (a, b) in H.cpcv_splits(T):
288	        best = choose_cell(T, masks, tr)
289	        oof_split[(a, b)] = (masks[best[2]][te] if best is not None else np.ones(len(te), dtype=bool)).astype(float)
290	    paths = H.cpcv_paths(T, oof_split)
291	    dist, path_rows = H.score_paths(T, paths, f"{STUDY}/nested", dict(selection="max diff | kept_share>=0.20 in training fold"), script=__file__, controls=True)
292	    log(f"  CPCV: {dist}")
293	    # the candidate: the cell chosen on all IS rows (its grid row is the ledger row)
294	    best_all = choose_cell(T, masks, is_rows)
295	    cand_cfg = json.loads(best_all[2]) if best_all else None
296	    res = next(r for r, k in zip(grid_rows, keys) if k == best_all[2]) if best_all else None
297	    fam = dict(pbo_diff=H.pbo(vecs, "diff"), pbo_kept_mean=H.pbo(vecs, "kept_mean"), spa=H.spa(vecs, tag=f"{STUDY}|{tf}"), effective_trials=H.effective_trials(vecs))
298	    go, checks, dsr, boot, combined = None, None, None, None, None
299	    if res is not None:
300	        vec = vecs[keys.index(best_all[2])]
301	        per = np.where(vec["kept_n"] > 0, vec["kept_sum"] / np.maximum(vec["kept_n"], 1), 0.0)[vec["kept_n"] > 0]
302	        srs = []
303	        for v in vecs:
304	            x = np.where(v["kept_n"] > 0, v["kept_sum"] / np.maximum(v["kept_n"], 1), 0.0)[v["kept_n"] > 0]
305	            if len(x) > 2 and x.std(ddof=1) > 0: srs.append(x.mean() / x.std(ddof=1))
306	        sr_var = float(np.var(srs, ddof=1)) if len(srs) > 1 and np.var(srs, ddof=1) > 0 else None
307	        dsr = H.deflated_sharpe(per, len(vecs), sr_var)
308	        boot = H.bootstrap_ci(vec, tag=f"{STUDY}|{tf}")
309	        go, checks = H.go_no_go(res, tf, cpcv=dist, pbo_value=fam["pbo_diff"]["pbo"], dsr=dsr, spa_p=fam["spa"]["spa_p"], boot=boot)
310	        log(f"  candidate {cand_cfg}: go={go} " + json.dumps(checks, default=str))
311	        comb = masks[best_all[2]] & T.F.fz_traded.astype(bool).to_numpy()
312	        combined = H.score(T, comb, f"{STUDY}/combined", dict(cand_cfg, and_gate="fz_traded (frozen ST7/ST8, comparator)"), script=__file__)
313	        log(f"  combined (rule AND fz_traded): id {combined['id']} kept {combined['kept_n']} diff {combined['diff']} ctrl {combined['control_pct']}")
314	    out.update(branch_b=dict(grid=[{k: r[k] for k in ("id", "config", "kept_n", "kept_share", "kept_mean", "skipped_mean", "diff", "diff_top1_removed", "perm_p", "control_pct",
315	                                                        "loser_recall", "loser_precision", "winner_recall_weighted", "top_decile_winners_skipped", "sign_blocks", "kept_mean_slip8")} for r in grid_rows],
316	                             nested_oof={k: nested[k] for k in ("id", "kept_n", "kept_share", "diff", "perm_p", "control_pct", "sign_blocks")}, chosen_per_fold=chosen_folds,
317	                             cpcv=dist, cpcv_path_ids=[r["id"] for r in path_rows], candidate=cand_cfg, candidate_ledger_id=res["id"] if res else None,
318	                             family=fam, dsr=dsr, bootstrap=boot, go_no_go=dict(passed=go, checks=checks) if checks else None,
319	                             combined={k: combined[k] for k in ("id", "kept_n", "kept_share", "diff", "perm_p", "control_pct", "sign_blocks")} if combined else None))

324	def selftest():

328	    assert np.allclose(tn, [0, -1000, -3500, -500, 0, -1200, -700]) and (ts == [0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1]).all()
329	    rm = running_min_by_session(tn, sess_first, sess_run); assert np.allclose(rm, [0, -1000, -3500, -3500, 0, -1200, -1200])
330	    assert (grid_keep(ts, rm, 1, None) == [1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0]).all()

332	    # rearm (k = 1): session 0 stops after position 1, position 2 is skipped and its paper trade wins -> re-armed, 3 taken;
333	    # session 1 stops after position 4, position 5 skipped and wins -> 6 taken

335	    assert (rearm_keep(net, stop, sess_first, sess_run, 1, None) != grid_keep(ts, rm, 1, None)).sum() == 2
336	    # rearm (k = 9, L = -3000): session 0 stops at position 1 (net -3500), 2 skipped and wins -> 3 taken; session 1 never stops
337	    assert (rearm_keep(net, stop, sess_first, sess_run, 9, -3000.0) == [1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1]).all()
338	    p = holm([0.01, 0.04, 0.03]); assert np.allclose(p, [0.03, 0.06, 0.06])
339	    s = stats7(tn, ts, net); assert np.isfinite(s[1]) and np.isnan(s[3])
340	    print("selftest ok")

11	Pre-registered (BRIEF.md + DESIGN_PANEL.md, fixed before any candidate was scored):
12	  unit        a Foundation SETUP with its own engine trade, taken under the book ST13/ST14 will trade: label L1 = the engine's
13	              stop / next-CHoCH exit cut at the entry session's 15:25 bar (lab.eod_cut), priced at lot 65, 5 pts slippage per
14	              side, lab.trade_charges(ZERODHA_NFO_FUT). A SETUP opening at or after 15:25 is not a unit (not taken). L0 (the
15	              engine's uncut trade) is a robustness label only.
16	  IS / OOS    IS = sessions 2021-10-01 .. 2025-12-31; OOS = 2026-01-01 .. 2026-09-25, opened once by oos_once.py alone.
17	  splitter    12 contiguous blocks of IS sessions (equal session counts); a training row is purged when its label lifetime
18	              [entry bar, exit bar] intersects the test block's bar range; 3 sessions after each test block are embargoed.
19	  CPCV        N = 12, k = 2: 66 splits, 11 paths; a candidate's path distribution (median, 5th percentile) is what counts.
20	  statistic   kept-vs-skipped mean net (INR per trade), never net alone (every skip saves ~1,100 INR of costs); the
21	              session-matched random control percentile (fz_report.random_control, 2,000 draws, seed 'fz'); the kept-vs-refused
22	              permutation p (fz_report.permutation_p); loser recall / precision; |net|-weighted winner recall; the top-decile
23	              winners skipped; the same difference with the top 1% winners removed; slippage 3 / 5 / 8 pts per side.
24	  ledger      append-only JSONL (ledger/trials.jsonl) + per-candidate per-session vectors (ledger/vectors/<id>.npz); PBO, DSR
25	              and SPA read the ledger, so every trial counts.
26	  go / no-go  PBO <= 0.2 over the family; CPCV 5th-percentile diff > 0; DSR p < 0.1; kept share >= 20%; kept n >= 300 (1m) /
27	              80 (5m); diff > 0 with the top 1% winners removed; the kept book's mean net > 0 at 8 pts slippage per side (the

71	    """One row per unit (a Foundation SETUP taken under the label's book), IS rows first in time order then OOS."""

73	    def __init__(self, tf, label, F, TR, sessions):
74	        self.tf, self.label, self.F, self.TR, self.sessions = tf, label, F, TR, sessions
75	        self.n = len(F)
76	        self.setup_i = F.setup_i.to_numpy()

88	        self.up = (F.dir.astype(str) == "up").to_numpy()

104	        out = np.empty(self.n)
105	        for i in range(self.n):

139	def design(T, cols=None, max_levels=MAX_LEVELS):
140	    """Numeric design matrix over as-of columns: floats as they are (None -> NaN), booleans 0 / 1, text one-hot (<= max_levels
141	    levels, else dropped). Returns (X DataFrame, {encoded column: source column})."""
142	    cols = list(cols) if cols is not None else T.asof_columns()
143	    out, src = {}, {}

145	        s = T.F[c]
146	        if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s): out[c] = s.astype(float).to_numpy(); src[c] = c; continue
147	        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s): out[c] = s.to_numpy(dtype=float); src[c] = c; continue
148	        so = s.astype(object)
149	        vals = so.map(lambda z: None if z is None or (isinstance(z, float) and np.isnan(z)) else z)
150	        if all(isinstance(z, (bool, np.bool_)) or z is None for z in vals):
151	            out[c] = vals.map(lambda z: np.nan if z is None else float(z)).to_numpy(dtype=float); src[c] = c; continue
152	        levels = sorted({str(z) for z in vals if z is not None})
153	        if len(levels) > max_levels: continue

167	        keep &= ~((e0 <= hi) & (e1 >= lo))
168	        keep &= ~np.isin(ses, list(T.block_embargo[b]))

172	def purged_splits(T):
173	    """12 (train_idx, test_idx) over IS rows: test = one block; train = the other blocks, purged and embargoed."""
174	    is_idx = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)

181	def cpcv_splits(T):
182	    """66 (train_idx, test_idx, (a, b)) with two test blocks each (N = 12, k = 2), purged against both and their embargoes."""
183	    is_idx = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
184	    for a, b in itertools.combinations(range(N_BLOCKS), CPCV_K):
185	        te = is_idx[np.isin(T.block[is_idx], [a, b])]
186	        tr = _purge(T, is_idx[~np.isin(T.block[is_idx], [a, b])], [a, b])
187	        yield tr, te, (a, b)

190	def cpcv_paths(T, oof_by_split):
191	    """11 backtest paths from the 66 CPCV splits. oof_by_split: {(a, b): array of decisions / scores for the rows of that
192	    split's test set, in the order cpcv_splits yields them}. Returns a list of 11 arrays over all rows (NaN outside IS): in
193	    path p, block g takes its prediction from the split that pairs g with its p-th other block."""
194	    is_idx = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
195	    paths = [np.full(T.n, np.nan) for _ in range(N_BLOCKS - 1)]
196	    for (a, b), pred in oof_by_split.items():
197	        te = is_idx[np.isin(T.block[is_idx], [a, b])]
198	        pred = np.asarray(pred, dtype=float); assert len(pred) == len(te), "prediction length must match the split's test rows"
199	        for g, other in ((a, b), (b, a)):
200	            p = [x for x in range(N_BLOCKS) if x != g].index(other)
201	            m = T.block[te] == g
202	            paths[p][te[m]] = pred[m]
203	    for p in paths: assert not np.isnan(p[is_idx]).any(), "every IS row must have a prediction in every path"
204	    return paths

207	def check_splits(T):
208	    """Leakage checks of the splitter: no training row's lifetime intersects its test block, no training row sits in the
209	    embargo, every IS row is tested once in the 12-block scheme; returns the counts."""
210	    n_te = np.zeros(T.n, dtype=int); purged = []
211	    for b, (tr, te) in enumerate(purged_splits(T)):
212	        lo, hi = T.block_range[b]
213	        assert not ((T.entry_bar[tr] <= hi) & (T.exit_bar[tr] >= lo)).any()
214	        assert not np.isin(T.session[tr], list(T.block_embargo[b])).any()
215	        assert (T.block[te] == b).all()
216	        n_te[te] += 1; purged.append(int(T.is_mask.sum() - len(te) - len(tr)))
217	    assert (n_te[T.is_mask] == 1).all() and (n_te[T.oos_mask] == 0).all()
218	    return dict(blocks=N_BLOCKS, rows_is=int(T.is_mask.sum()), rows_oos=int(T.oos_mask.sum()), purged_per_block=purged,
219	                block_sessions=[len(bs) for bs in T.block_sessions], block_rows=[int((T.block == b).sum()) for b in range(N_BLOCKS)],

238	def metrics(T, keep, rows, tag, controls=True, draws=CONTROL_DRAWS):
239	    """Kept-vs-skipped metrics of a boolean keep mask over the rows `rows` of T (a subset of one split)."""
240	    keep = np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)
241	    k = rows[keep[rows]]; s = rows[~keep[rows]]
242	    net, win = T.net, T.win
243	    nk, ns = len(k), len(s)
244	    m = dict(n=int(len(rows)), kept_n=int(nk), skipped_n=int(ns), kept_share=round(nk / len(rows), 4) if len(rows) else None,
245	             kept_net=round(float(net[k].sum()), 2), skipped_net=round(float(net[s].sum()), 2),
246	             kept_mean=round(float(net[k].mean()), 2) if nk else None, skipped_mean=round(float(net[s].mean()), 2) if ns else None,
247	             all_mean=round(float(net[rows].mean()), 2) if len(rows) else None,
248	             kept_win_rate=round(float(win[k].mean()), 4) if nk else None, skipped_win_rate=round(float(win[s].mean()), 4) if ns else None,
249	             kept_pf=None, kept_t=None, diff=None, diff_top1_removed=None, kept_mean_slip3=None, kept_mean_slip8=None,
250	             loser_recall=None, loser_precision=None, winner_recall=None, winner_recall_weighted=None, top_decile_winners_skipped=None,
251	             kept_sessions=int(len(set(T.session[k].tolist()))), sign_blocks=None, perm_p=None, control_pct=None, control_p_beat=None)
252	    if nk:
253	        w_, l_ = net[k][net[k] > 0], net[k][net[k] <= 0]
254	        m["kept_pf"] = round(float(w_.sum() / -l_.sum()), 3) if len(l_) and l_.sum() else None
255	        m["kept_t"] = round(float(net[k].mean() / (net[k].std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(nk))), 2) if nk > 1 and net[k].std(ddof=1) else None
256	    if nk and ns:
257	        m["diff"] = round(float(net[k].mean() - net[s].mean()), 2)
258	        # slippage moves every trade's net by the same amount, so the kept-vs-skipped difference is invariant; what a marginal
259	        # gate must survive is the kept book's own expectancy at 3 / 8 pts per side
260	        for sl_ in (3.0, 8.0): m[f"kept_mean_slip{int(sl_)}"] = round(float(T.net_slip[sl_][k].mean()), 2)
261	        top = np.quantile(net[rows], 0.99); kk, ss_ = k[net[k] < top], s[net[s] < top]
262	        m["diff_top1_removed"] = round(float(net[kk].mean() - net[ss_].mean()), 2) if len(kk) and len(ss_) else None
263	        L = ~win[rows]; W = win[rows]
264	        skp = ~keep[rows]
265	        m["loser_recall"] = round(float((skp & L).sum() / L.sum()), 4) if L.sum() else None
266	        m["loser_precision"] = round(float((skp & L).sum() / skp.sum()), 4) if skp.sum() else None
267	        m["winner_recall"] = round(float((~skp & W).sum() / W.sum()), 4) if W.sum() else None
268	        wn = net[rows]
269	        m["winner_recall_weighted"] = round(float(wn[~skp & W].sum() / wn[W].sum()), 4) if W.sum() and wn[W].sum() else None
270	        if W.sum():
271	            q = np.quantile(wn[W], 0.9); big = W & (wn >= q)
272	            m["top_decile_winners_skipped"] = round(float((skp & big).sum() / big.sum()), 4) if big.sum() else None
273	        bl = T.block[rows]
274	        if (bl >= 0).all():
275	            m["sign_blocks"] = int(sum(1 for b in range(N_BLOCKS) if (keep[rows] & (bl == b)).sum() and (~keep[rows] & (bl == b)).sum()
276	                                      and net[rows][keep[rows] & (bl == b)].mean() > net[rows][~keep[rows] & (bl == b)].mean()))
277	        if controls:
278	            pp = fz_report.permutation_p(net[k].tolist(), net[s].tolist(), draws, SEED, tag)
279	            m["perm_p"] = pp["p"]
280	            rc = fz_report.random_control(_units(T, rows), _units(T, k, "SEL"), draws, SEED, tag)
281	            m["control_pct"], m["control_p_beat"], m["control_p50"] = rc["fz_pct"], rc["p_beat"], rc["p50"]
282	    return m

285	def session_vectors(T, keep, rows):
286	    """Per active session (sessions with a unit among rows): kept sum / n, skipped sum / n, all sum / n."""
287	    keep = np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)
288	    ses = T.session[rows]; net = T.net[rows]; kp = keep[rows]
289	    S = np.array(sorted(set(ses.tolist())))
290	    idx = np.searchsorted(S, ses)
291	    out = {}
292	    for name, msk in (("kept", kp), ("skipped", ~kp), ("all", np.ones(len(rows), dtype=bool))):
293	        out[name + "_sum"] = np.bincount(idx, weights=net * msk, minlength=len(S))
294	        out[name + "_n"] = np.bincount(idx, weights=msk.astype(float), minlength=len(S))
295	    out["sessions"] = S
296	    return out

358	def _partitions(S=CSCV_S):
359	    """All C(S, S/2) IS / pseudo-OOS block assignments as a boolean matrix (partitions x S), True = in-sample half."""
360	    combs = list(itertools.combinations(range(S), S // 2))
361	    M = np.zeros((len(combs), S), dtype=bool)
362	    for i, cmb in enumerate(combs): M[i, list(cmb)] = True
363	    return M

366	def pbo(vectors, statistic="kept_mean", S=CSCV_S):
367	    """CSCV probability of backtest overfitting (Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado & Zhu 2017) over a family of candidates.
368	    vectors: list of session_vectors dicts (one per candidate, same sessions). Each candidate's per-session series is split into
369	    S contiguous blocks; for every C(S, S/2) partition the IS-best candidate's OOS rank is recorded; PBO = share of partitions
370	    where that rank is below the median (logit < 0). statistic: 'kept_mean' = kept net per kept trade over the half, or 'diff'
371	    = kept mean minus skipped mean over the half. Also the IS-vs-OOS performance degradation slope and the share of partitions
372	    where the IS-best is below zero OOS."""
373	    M = len(vectors)
374	    if M < 2: return dict(candidates=M, pbo=None, note="needs at least 2 candidates")
375	    T_ = len(vectors[0]["sessions"]); edges = np.linspace(0, T_, S + 1).round().astype(int)
376	    def blocks(v, key):
377	        return np.array([v[key][edges[b]:edges[b + 1]].sum() for b in range(S)])
378	    KS = np.array([blocks(v, "kept_sum") for v in vectors]); KN = np.array([blocks(v, "kept_n") for v in vectors])
379	    SS = np.array([blocks(v, "skipped_sum") for v in vectors]); SN = np.array([blocks(v, "skipped_n") for v in vectors])
380	    P = _partitions(S).astype(float)                                           # partitions x S
381	    def perf(Pm):
382	        ks, kn = Pm @ KS.T, Pm @ KN.T                                           # partitions x M
383	        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
384	            km = np.where(kn > 0, ks / kn, np.nan)
385	            if statistic == "kept_mean": return km
386	            ss, sn = Pm @ SS.T, Pm @ SN.T
387	            return km - np.where(sn > 0, ss / sn, np.nan)
388	    ins, oos = perf(P), perf(1 - P)
389	    ins = np.where(np.isnan(ins), -np.inf, ins)
390	    best = np.argmax(ins, axis=1)
391	    oos_best = oos[np.arange(len(P)), best]
392	    ranks = np.array([(np.nan_to_num(oos[i], nan=-np.inf) < oos_best[i]).sum() / (M - 1) if M > 1 else 0.5 for i in range(len(P))])
393	    ranks = np.clip(ranks, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
394	    logit = np.log(ranks / (1 - ranks))
395	    ins_best = ins[np.arange(len(P)), best]
396	    ok = np.isfinite(oos_best) & np.isfinite(ins_best)
397	    slope = float(np.polyfit(ins_best[ok], oos_best[ok], 1)[0]) if ok.sum() > 2 else None
398	    return dict(candidates=M, partitions=int(len(P)), statistic=statistic, pbo=round(float((logit < 0).mean()), 4),
399	                oos_best_below_zero=round(float((oos_best[ok] < 0).mean()), 4) if ok.any() else None,
400	                degradation_slope=round(slope, 4) if slope is not None else None,
401	                is_best_mean=round(float(ins_best[ok].mean()), 2) if ok.any() else None,
402	                oos_best_mean=round(float(oos_best[ok].mean()), 2) if ok.any() else None)
403

405	def effective_trials(vectors, key="kept_sum"):
406	    """Participation-ratio count of independent trials from the correlation matrix of the candidates' per-session series."""
407	    X = np.array([v[key] for v in vectors], dtype=float)
408	    X = X[:, X.std(axis=0) > 0] if X.shape[0] > 1 else X
409	    if X.shape[0] < 2: return float(X.shape[0])
410	    C = np.corrcoef(X); C = np.nan_to_num(C, nan=0.0); np.fill_diagonal(C, 1.0)
411	    lam = np.clip(np.linalg.eigvalsh(C), 0, None)
412	    return round(float(lam.sum() ** 2 / (lam ** 2).sum()), 2)

415	def deflated_sharpe(per_session, n_trials, sr_var_trials=None):
416	    """Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014): the probability that the per-session Sharpe of a book is above the expected maximum
417	    Sharpe of n_trials trials with variance sr_var_trials (the variance of Sharpe across the family; estimated from
418	    per_session's own scale when None), with the skew / kurtosis correction. Returns SR, SR0, DSR, p = 1 - DSR."""
419	    x = np.asarray(per_session, dtype=float); T_ = len(x)
420	    if T_ < 3 or x.std(ddof=1) == 0: return dict(sr=None, sr0=None, dsr=None, p=None, T=T_)
421	    sr = float(x.mean() / x.std(ddof=1)); g3 = float(sst.skew(x)); g4 = float(sst.kurtosis(x, fisher=False))
422	    V = sr_var_trials if sr_var_trials is not None else 1.0 / T_
423	    N = max(2, n_trials); em = 0.5772156649
424	    sr0 = math.sqrt(V) * ((1 - em) * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / N) + em * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / (N * math.e)))
425	    den = 1 - g3 * sr + (g4 - 1) / 4 * sr * sr
426	    if den <= 0: return dict(sr=round(sr, 4), sr0=round(sr0, 4), dsr=None, p=None, T=T_, note="denominator <= 0")
427	    z = (sr - sr0) * math.sqrt(T_ - 1) / math.sqrt(den)
428	    dsr = float(sst.norm.cdf(z))
429	    return dict(sr=round(sr, 4), sr0=round(float(sr0), 4), dsr=round(dsr, 4), p=round(1 - dsr, 4), T=T_, n_trials=n_trials, skew=round(g3, 3), kurt=round(g4, 3))
430

432	def min_backtest_length(sr, n_trials, sr_var_trials):
433	    """Sessions needed for the observed per-session Sharpe to clear the expected maximum of n_trials (AFML 14.7)."""
434	    N = max(2, n_trials); em = 0.5772156649
435	    sr0 = math.sqrt(sr_var_trials) * ((1 - em) * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / N) + em * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / (N * math.e)))
436	    return round(float((sr0 / sr) ** 2 + 1), 1) if sr > 0 else None

439	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- resampling: stationary block bootstrap of sessions, SPA
440	def stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, mean_block=BOOT_MEAN_BLOCK, seed=SEED, tag=""):
441	    """Politis & Romano stationary bootstrap indices (draws x T_) over T_ ordered sessions; seeded and reproducible."""
442	    rng = np.random.default_rng(int(_sha(f"{seed}|boot|{tag}"), 16) % (2 ** 32))
443	    p = 1.0 / mean_block
444	    starts = rng.integers(0, T_, size=(draws, T_)); cont = rng.random((draws, T_)) >= p
445	    idx = np.empty((draws, T_), dtype=int)
446	    idx[:, 0] = starts[:, 0]
447	    for t_ in range(1, T_):
448	        idx[:, t_] = np.where(cont[:, t_], (idx[:, t_ - 1] + 1) % T_, starts[:, t_])
449	    return idx

452	def bootstrap_ci(vec, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, ci=GO["boot_ci"], tag=""):
453	    """Block-bootstrap CI (sessions resampled) of the kept-vs-skipped difference and of the kept mean from a session_vectors dict."""
454	    T_ = len(vec["sessions"]); idx = stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws, tag=tag)
455	    ks, kn, ss, sn = (vec[k][idx].sum(axis=1) for k in ("kept_sum", "kept_n", "skipped_sum", "skipped_n"))
456	    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
457	        km = np.where(kn > 0, ks / kn, np.nan); sm = np.where(sn > 0, ss / sn, np.nan); d = km - sm
458	    a = (1 - ci) / 2
459	    q = lambda v: [round(float(np.nanquantile(v, a)), 2), round(float(np.nanquantile(v, 1 - a)), 2)]
460	    return dict(draws=draws, ci=ci, diff_ci=q(d), kept_mean_ci=q(km), diff_p_le0=round(float(np.nanmean(d <= 0)), 4),
461	                diff_point=round(float(np.nansum(vec["kept_sum"]) / max(1, vec["kept_n"].sum()) - np.nansum(vec["skipped_sum"]) / max(1, vec["skipped_n"].sum())), 2))

464	def selection_gain(vec):
465	    """Per-session selection gain d_t = kept mean in session t minus the session's mean over all units (0 when nothing kept):
466	    the per-session statistic behind the session-matched random control (its expectation under random selection is 0)."""
467	    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
468	        km = np.where(vec["kept_n"] > 0, vec["kept_sum"] / vec["kept_n"], np.nan)
469	        am = vec["all_sum"] / vec["all_n"]
470	    d = km - am
471	    return np.where(np.isnan(d), 0.0, d), vec["kept_n"] > 0

474	def spa(vectors, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, tag=""):
475	    """White's Reality Check and Hansen's SPA over a family of candidates: H0 = no candidate has positive expected selection
476	    gain (per-session kept mean minus the session mean). Stationary bootstrap of sessions, studentised statistics, Hansen's
477	    consistent recentring. Returns the best candidate's statistic and the RC / SPA p-values."""
478	    Dm = np.array([selection_gain(v)[0] for v in vectors], dtype=float)       # M x T
479	    M, T_ = Dm.shape
480	    mu = Dm.mean(axis=1); se = Dm.std(axis=1, ddof=1) / math.sqrt(T_); se = np.where(se > 0, se, np.inf)
481	    tstat = np.sqrt(T_) * mu / (Dm.std(axis=1, ddof=1) + 1e-12)
482	    idx = stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws, tag=tag)
483	    best = int(np.argmax(tstat)); rc_stat = float(tstat[best])
484	    # bootstrap of the max studentised statistic under the recentred null
485	    mub = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].mean(axis=1) for d in range(draws)])           # draws x M
486	    sdb = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].std(axis=1, ddof=1) for d in range(draws)]) + 1e-12
487	    rc_max = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu) / sdb, axis=1)                       # White: recentre at the sample mean
488	    thr = np.sqrt(np.var(Dm, axis=1, ddof=1) / T_ * 2 * math.log(math.log(T_)))
489	    mu_c = np.where(mu < -thr, mu, 0.0)                                            # Hansen's consistent recentring
490	    spa_max = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu + mu_c) / sdb, axis=1)
491	    return dict(candidates=M, sessions=T_, best=best, best_mean_gain=round(float(mu[best]), 2), best_t=round(rc_stat, 3),
492	                rc_p=round(float((rc_max >= rc_stat).mean()), 4), spa_p=round(float((spa_max >= rc_stat).mean()), 4), draws=draws)

495	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- structural breaks of the book's own expectancy
496	def _hac_var(x, lag=5):
497	    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float) - np.mean(x); T_ = len(x)
498	    s = float((x * x).sum())
499	    for k in range(1, lag + 1):
500	        w = 1 - k / (lag + 1); s += 2 * w * float((x[k:] * x[:-k]).sum())
501	    return s / T_ / T_                                                             # variance of the mean

504	def chow_mean(x, y, lag=5):
505	    """HAC (Newey-West, Bartlett, lag 5) t-test of a difference of means between two consecutive segments."""
506	    x, y = np.asarray(x, dtype=float), np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
507	    if len(x) < 5 or len(y) < 5: return dict(t=None, p=None, n=[len(x), len(y)])
508	    t_ = (y.mean() - x.mean()) / math.sqrt(_hac_var(x, lag) + _hac_var(y, lag))
509	    return dict(t=round(float(t_), 3), p=round(float(2 * (1 - sst.norm.cdf(abs(t_)))), 4), mean_before=round(float(x.mean()), 2),
510	                mean_after=round(float(y.mean()), 2), n=[len(x), len(y)])

513	def bde_cusum(x, k=10):
514	    """Brown-Durbin-Evans CUSUM of recursive residuals of the constant-mean model on the ordered series x: the maximum
515	    crossing of the 5% bands +-0.948 sqrt(T-k) (1 + 2 (r-k)/(T-k)); reports whether the path leaves the band and where."""
516	    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float); T_ = len(x)
517	    if T_ <= k + 2: return dict(break_detected=None)
518	    w = np.array([(x[t_] - x[:t_].mean()) / math.sqrt(1 + 1 / t_) for t_ in range(k, T_)])
519	    sig = w.std(ddof=1)
520	    W = np.cumsum(w) / sig
521	    r = np.arange(k + 1, T_ + 1)
522	    band = 0.948 * math.sqrt(T_ - k) * (1 + 2 * (r - k) / (T_ - k))
523	    ex = np.abs(W) > band
524	    return dict(break_detected=bool(ex.any()), first_crossing_index=int(np.argmax(ex)) + k if ex.any() else None,
525	                max_ratio=round(float(np.max(np.abs(W) / band)), 3), T=T_)

528	def break_tests(T, lag=5):
529	    """The pre-registration step: has the book's per-session expectancy (active sessions, label L1) changed inside IS or at the
530	    IS / OOS boundary? Rolling 60-session mean with block-bootstrap bands, BDE CUSUM, HAC Chow tests per calendar year, and the
531	    one permitted OOS aggregate read: the Chow test at 2026-01-01 (it decides the OOS caveat, never a key)."""
532	    rows = np.arange(T.n)
533	    ses = T.session[rows]; net = T.net[rows]
534	    S = np.array(sorted(set(ses.tolist()))); idx = np.searchsorted(S, ses)
535	    per = np.bincount(idx, weights=net, minlength=len(S)) / np.bincount(idx, minlength=len(S))
536	    day = dict(zip(T.session, T.day)); days = np.array([day[int(s)] for s in S])
537	    is_ = days <= IS_END
538	    x_is = per[is_]
539	    years = sorted({d[:4] for d in days[is_]})
540	    chow_years = {}
541	    for y in years[1:]:
542	        before = x_is[np.array([d[:4] < y for d in days[is_]])]; after = x_is[np.array([d[:4] == y for d in days[is_]])]
543	        chow_years[y] = chow_mean(before, after, lag)
544	    boundary = chow_mean(x_is, per[~is_], lag)
545	    roll = pd.Series(x_is).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy()
546	    idxb = stationary_bootstrap_idx(len(x_is), 500, tag="roll")
547	    rb = np.array([pd.Series(x_is[idxb[d]]).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy() for d in range(500)])
548	    lo, hi = np.nanquantile(rb, 0.05, axis=0), np.nanquantile(rb, 0.95, axis=0)
549	    outside = int(np.nansum((roll < lo) | (roll > hi)))
550	    return dict(label=T.label, active_is_sessions=int(is_.sum()), is_mean_per_session=round(float(x_is.mean()), 2),
551	                bde=bde_cusum(x_is), chow_per_year=chow_years, chow_is_oos_boundary=boundary,
552	                rolling60_outside_band=outside, rolling60_points=int(np.isfinite(roll).sum()),
553	                winners_only_boundary=chow_mean(x_is[x_is > 0], per[~is_][per[~is_] > 0], lag) if (per[~is_] > 0).sum() >= 5 else None,
554	                caveat=("IS/OOS boundary Chow p < 0.05: the OOS window is not from the same process; every OOS table carries this"
555	                        if boundary["p"] is not None and boundary["p"] < 0.05 else "no boundary break at 5%"))

186	**Reading.** 31 of 32 cells have a positive pooled `diff` (range -4 to +120 INR/trade) and every cell sits at the **0.0th percentile** of the session-matched random control (best sign count 10/12 blocks). The two disagree because they measure different things: the pooled difference mixes sessions, and the kept set is enriched with the rows of short sessions (1-3 SETUPs, where the rule never binds), which are the trending days with the best expectancy, while the skipped rows all come from long, choppy sessions; the control draws the same number of positions inside each session and removes that composition. Within a session the rule keeps the first SETUPs, and by construction the trade that triggered the stop (a stop-loss or the loss that took the ledger past L) is always in the kept set, while the skipped later SETUPs are the ones the null test showed to be less bad than their peers. The rule therefore does worse than picking the same number of same-session SETUPs at random in essentially every draw. Judged as the design requires (kept-vs-skipped at matched per-session k and the control), no cell has an edge; the positive pooled diff is cost avoidance plus session composition.

303	- **Falsifiers of the memory claim.** Mixed signs of the N1 excess across the six threshold tests, or a min Holm p above 0.05 under N1, would remove the "session memory beyond the hour effect" statement; the L0 table (section 3) is the robustness check and its signs / p are reported above. 304	- **Falsifiers of the no-key conclusion.** Any grid cell with control percentile >= 95 together with a CPCV 5th-percentile diff > 0 and PBO <= 0.2 would reopen the rule; none is close (max control pct 0.0). The pooled `diff` is positive for every cell and must not be read as edge: the kept set is enriched with short-session (trending-day) rows and always contains the triggering loser.
305	- **p definition.** The doubled-tail permutation p replaced the naive |stat| form after a 50-draw timing probe on 1 min / L1 showed the N1 distribution off centre (it is the wrong hypothesis to test |stat| against zero when the null itself is not centred at zero); nothing else changed and no full run preceded the change (`preregistration.json`, `p_definition_history`). 306	- **Ledger semantics.** `today_*_asof` counts trades with entry < k and exit <= k (verified identical on the truncated build); on this book it equals the cumulative prior outcomes of the session's units (asserted in code), so the permutation null recomputes it exactly. Before the first trigger the strategy's own ledger equals Foundation's, so the absorbing replay is exact; the rearm variant's "winner" is the paper trade of a skipped SETUP (the lab tracks every Foundation SETUP, so it is observable live).
307	- **Composition.** Sessions with many SETUPs are the choppy days; any rule keyed on the ledger inherits the session-count composition. The session-matched control is the yardstick that removes it; the pooled difference does not.

"""Refuter check: does a MEMORYLESS process with outcome-dependent trade duration reject the study's N1 null?"""
import sys, os, json, time, numpy as np, pandas as pd
OUT="/home/user/money-maker/research/strategy_lab/fz_v3/out"; sys.path.insert(0, OUT); sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
import harness as H, fz_report
import ss_copy as SS
t0=time.time()
T=H.load("minute","L1"); rows=np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask); S=SS.session_frame(T, rows)
F=T.F.iloc[rows]
B=pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(OUT,"data/minute/bars.parquet"), columns=["i","datetime","session_idx"])
hhmm=B.datetime.astype(str).str[11:16].to_numpy(); sess_of_bar=B.session_idx.to_numpy()
def hbin(h): return "<09:25" if h<"09:25" else ">=15:20" if h>="15:20" else h[:2]
# per-session cut bar (15:25) and real first SETUP bar
cut={}
for s, g in B.groupby("session_idx"):
    m=g[g.datetime.astype(str).str[11:16]=="15:25"]
    cut[int(s)]=int(m.i.iloc[0]) if len(m) else int(g.i.iloc[-1])
first_setup=F.groupby("session_idx").setup_i.min().to_dict()
# pools
net=S["net"]; stop=S["stop"]; dur=(F.l1_exit_i.to_numpy()-F.setup_i.to_numpy()).astype(int); hb=S["hour_bin"]
pool={h: np.flatnonzero(hb==h) for h in np.unique(hb)}
sess=S["sess"]; setup=T.setup_i[rows]; exit_=F.l1_exit_i.to_numpy().astype(int)
nxt_same=np.r_[sess[1:]==sess[:-1], False]
gaps=(np.r_[setup[1:],0]-exit_)[nxt_same]; gaps=gaps[gaps>=1]
print("real: units", len(rows), "gap pool", len(gaps), "median gap", np.median(gaps))

def simulate(seed, dur_independent=False):
    rng=np.random.default_rng(seed)
    recs=[]
    for s in sorted(set(sess.tolist())):
        t=int(first_setup[s]); c=cut[s]
        while t < c:
            h=hbin(hhmm[t]); p=pool[h]
            j=p[rng.integers(len(p))]
            d = dur[p[rng.integers(len(p))]] if dur_independent else dur[j]
            recs.append((s, h, net[j], bool(stop[j])))
            ex=min(t+max(int(d),1), c)
            t=ex+int(gaps[rng.integers(len(gaps))])
    df=pd.DataFrame(recs, columns=["sess","hb","net","stop"])
    ss=df.sess.to_numpy(); hb_=df.hb.to_numpy(); n_=df.net.to_numpy(float); st=df.stop.to_numpy(bool)
    new_sess=np.r_[True, ss[1:]!=ss[:-1]]; sess_run=np.cumsum(new_sess)-1
    new_cell=new_sess | np.r_[True, hb_[1:]!=hb_[:-1]]; cell_run=np.cumsum(new_cell)-1
    sess_first=np.flatnonzero(new_sess)
    tn, ts=SS.recompute_ledger(n_, st, sess_first, sess_run)
    return dict(rows=np.arange(len(df)), sess=ss, hour_bin=hb_, net=n_, stop=st, today_net=tn, today_stops=ts, sess_run=sess_run, cell_run=cell_run, sess_first=sess_first, win=n_>0)

def report(tag, Ssim, draws=2000):
    R=SS.null_test(Ssim, "minute", "L1", "session_x_hour", draws=draws)
    cnt=np.bincount(Ssim["cell_run"]); multi=cnt[Ssim["cell_run"]]>1; last=np.r_[Ssim["cell_run"][1:]!=Ssim["cell_run"][:-1], True]
    g=pd.Series(Ssim["sess"]).value_counts()
    print(f"\n== {tag}: units {len(Ssim['net'])} sessions {len(g)} median/session {g.median():.0f} max {g.max()} | cells {R['n_cells']} singletons {R['cells_size1']} movable {R['rows_movable']} | win rate {Ssim['win'].mean():.4f} mean net {Ssim['net'].mean():.1f}")
    print(f"   win rate last-in-multi-cell {Ssim['win'][multi&last].mean():.4f} vs not-last {Ssim['win'][multi&~last].mean():.4f}")
    tab=pd.DataFrame(dict(test=SS.TESTS, observed=R["observed"].round(4), N1_mean=R["perm_mean"].round(4), N1_sd=R["perm_sd"].round(4), excess=R["excess"].round(4), p=R["p"].round(4), p_holm=R["p_holm"].round(4)))
    print(tab.to_string(index=False)); print(f"   min Holm p {R['p_holm'].min():.4f} -> rejected: {R['p_holm'].min()<0.05}")
    # the k=2 / L=None absorbing rule on the synthetic stream: pooled diff and the session-matched random control
    runmin=SS.running_min_by_session(Ssim["today_net"], Ssim["sess_first"], Ssim["sess_run"])
    keep=SS.grid_keep(Ssim["today_stops"], runmin, 2, None)
    n_=Ssim["net"]; diff=n_[keep].mean()-n_[~keep].mean()
    raw=[dict(day=str(s), net=float(v)) for s,v in zip(Ssim["sess"], n_)]; sel=[u for u,k in zip(raw, keep) if k]
    rc=fz_report.random_control(raw, sel, 2000, "fz", f"refute|{tag}")
    print(f"   rule k=2 L=None: kept {keep.sum()} share {keep.mean():.3f} pooled diff {diff:+.1f} | session-matched control pct {rc['fz_pct']} (p_beat {rc['p_beat']})")
    return R

for seed in (11, 22):
    report(f"memoryless, duration tied to outcome, seed {seed}", simulate(seed))
report("memoryless, duration INDEPENDENT of outcome, seed 33", simulate(33, dur_independent=True))
print(f"\ndone {time.time()-t0:.0f}s")
EOF

issues.what: The study's primary reported finding, 'pre-registered null N1 rejected on 1 min: session memory beyond the hour effect, mean-reverting (+53..+106 INR/trade excess)', is a false positive produced by a mis-specified null, not evidence of memory. N1 fixes the SETUP positions and permutes outcomes within session x hour_bin cells, but the positions are generated by the outcomes: a Foundation trade runs until exit and the next SETUP can only occur after it (ledger identity asserted at session_stop.py:94-95; min gap exit->next SETUP = 1 bar), and winners hold ~6x longer than losers. So within a multi-member cell the early units are losers almost by construction and a long winner is the last unit; shuffling outcomes across fixed positions puts winners at rank 0, which the observed data almost never does, and the observed stat is mechanically above the permutation distribution in exactly the 'mean-reverting' direction. A process with ZERO memory reproduces every reported number.
issues.where: /home/user/money-maker/research/strategy_lab/fz_v3/out/studies/session_stop/session_stop.py:17-19 (docstring: 'positions fixed ... so a rejection is session memory beyond the hour effect') and :127-147 (null_test: perm = np.lexsort((rng.random(len(cell)), cell)), outcomes permuted over fixed positions); FINDINGS.md:7, :80-82 ('there is session memory beyond the hour effect'), :308 (follow-up 'reverse rule' hypothesis); findings.json fields direction, session_memory_null_rejected, headline; the reported key_numbers 'excess_beyond_hour_effect_inr' and 'direction: MEAN-REVERTING'.
issues.evidence: Real IS data (minute/L1, 4,452 units): l1 bars held win mean 110.6 (median 75.5) vs loss 18.7 (median 12.0), stop-loss exits 8.2; P(another unit follows in the session | win) 0.571 vs | loss 0.925; in multi-member session x hour cells the LAST unit wins 23.1% vs 1.5% for non-last units (rank-0 units 1.8%), mean net -595 vs -1,828; last unit of a multi-unit session wins 47.6% vs 10.2%. Simulation (scratchpad sim_memoryless.py, 2,000 draws, the study's own null_test/recompute_ledger/stats7 code): outcomes drawn iid within hour_bin from the real pool (no memory by construction), duration = the drawn unit's real duration, gaps from the empirical distribution, on the real 578-session skeleton -> seeds 11/22: units 4,624/4,542, all 7 tests reject N1 with Holm p <= 0.009, threshold excess +59..+118 INR/trade, Spearman excess -0.0216/-0.0203, last-in-cell win rate 0.248/0.240 vs 0.028/0.022 (real: excess +53..+106, Spearman -0.0233, Holm <= 0.014, 0.231 vs 0.015).
